newsitem.title: GERMANY: Coffee consumers, producers seen cutting stocks.
newsitem.headline: Coffee consumers, producers seen cutting stocks.

text.p: Coffee importing and producing countries are set to draw down their stocks in the tight 1996/97 season, figures from German trader Bernhard Rothfos GmbH showed.
Rothfos put end-season stocks in producing countries at 22.8 million bags on Oct 1, 1997, down 1.4 million bags from a year earlier.

Drawdowns within the American milds group itself would constitute two million bags alone, it noted. This would be a result of efforts by Colombia, Costa Rica and El Salvador to achieve their milds export goals.
A small decrease was also seen in the African and Asian milds category. However, stocks of unwashed arabicas, including Brazil government stocks and those of robustas, should rise.
Consumer countries stocks in 96/97 should fall by 612,000 bags to 7.66 million on Oct 1, Rothfos said.
The new figure would represent 5.3 weeks of coverage, a level "dangerously below the accepted minimum required by the industry," it said.
